why: git treats a UTF-16 file as binary (numstat prints a dash, git grep misses it), so a UTF-16 CLAUDE.md is invisible to diff review while the agent decodes it fine. Measured: a naive UTF-8 read of such a file finds 0 of 12 hidden code points and a BOM decode finds all 12. Both sides are CLAUDE.md in UTF-16LE with a byte order mark; the fail side has U+200B inside a word. Decode without the BOM, or skip what git calls binary, and the fail side goes green; read the bytes as UTF-8, find the NUL half of every code unit and call the agent file unreadable, and the pass side goes red.
